one_month_reasoning: Arista's Q3 2026 date is not yet announced (no 8-K as of Sep 30). Its last three reports were on Tuesdays, so Tue Nov 3 is most likely; either Nov 2 or Nov 3 falls OUTSIDE the 2026-10-30 window. Inside the window are the late-October hyperscaler Q3 prints and 2027 capex remarks. Microsoft (26% of FY2025 revenue) and Meta (16%) matter most, and the read-through can go either way. FOMC and macro prints are also in the window. With no company event, I centre a near-symmetric lognormal on ~$205 (spot plus a trace of momentum). I cut the monthly sigma from 15% to ~14%, since realized vol over the last 20/40 days is 40-45%, below the 54% one-year figure. A month out, valuation does not drive the price.

fair_value.method: The forward P/E leg is NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of ~$5.86 (0.25 x FY27 consensus $5.20 + 0.75 x FY28 ~$6.08) x 35x = $205, weight 0.6. The FCF-yield leg is FY28 FCF ~$7.3B at a 3.25% yield plus ~$15/share projected horizon net cash = $191, weight 0.4. The blend is ~$200.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 ~$5.86 (0.25 x FY27 $5.20 + 0.75 x FY28 $6.08) x 35x forward P/E

inputs_detail.value: $5.20 (29 analysts, range $4.66-5.73; revised up 16% in 60 days)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus $5.20 x 1.17. Morningstar models ~20% 2028 revenue growth, and UBS/Goldman see hyperscaler capex growth slowing to ~6-12% in 2028, so I trim to 17%. Gross margin is guided 'margin neutral', so EPS grows roughly with revenue.

The 5-year average forward P/E is ~34x. My own-history base rate says that when ANET started at an NTM P/E of 30-38x, the median next-12m return was only +13% (n=31 months, P(<0) 29%). Above 38x, the stock has almost no history (2 months). Spot is ~41x NTM. With growth slowing from ~40% to ~20-25%, I assume the multiple moves back to about its average.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 revenue ~$19.2B x 38% FCF margin = ~$7.3B; at a 3.25% yield = ~$225B / 1.276B shares = $176, plus ~$15/share projected Sep-2027 net cash

inputs_detail.derivation: H1 2026 OCF of $2.78B on $5.74B revenue (48%) includes a $1.49B deferred-revenue build. Excluding it, OCF was only ~22%, depressed by inventory and other-asset builds against $9.7B of purchase commitments. Deferred revenue is real customer cash, but it can unwind once acceptances clear, so I use neither extreme. I take 38%: below the ~46% GAAP operating margin (tax and working capital) and above the ex-deferred H1 figure, on the view that inventory builds normalise as supply constraints ease. This is my judgment, and the leg carries the lower weight for that reason.
~31x FCF, in line with a ~34-35x historical forward P/E for ~20% growth with capex-cycle exposure.
$2,290.2M cash + $11,053.1M marketable securities = $13.34B, plus ~5 quarters of ~$1.3-1.5B normalised FCF, less modest buybacks (~$818M authorisation left).

bear.story: Hyperscaler capex growth slows faster than consensus (UBS path), or Microsoft/Meta cut or reallocate spending. IDC share loss to Nvidia continues (2Q26 Nvidia 20.4% vs Arista 18.7% of branded DC Ethernet), and some of the $6.87B deferred revenue unwinds slowly. EPS ends near ~$4.8 NTM and the multiple mean-reverts to ~25-26x. This matches ANET's own history of 40-55% peak-to-trough drawdowns (2018-19, 2022, early 2025).

base.story: FY27 is delivered close to the $5.20 consensus (~27% growth) and the stock enters FY28 at ~20% growth. The forward multiple compresses from ~41x toward ~36-37x, so the price ends slightly above spot. That fits the conditioned base rate (median +13% from a 30-38x start, and less from 41x).

bull.story: On the Goldman path (hyperscaler capex +54% in 2027), deferred AI revenue converts and Arista wins back back-end share (Dell'Oro says it is near-tied once deferred revenue is counted). EPS beats and FY28 is seen at ~$6.8+, with the multiple holding ~42-43x. The price is capped below round 1's $310 because a 40x+ start has almost no historical precedent for further expansion.

thesis_break_reason: $140 is ~31% below spot and ~27x FY27 consensus EPS ($5.20), well under the ~34x five-year average forward multiple. Reaching it most likely takes a fundamental break: a Microsoft/Meta capex cut or share loss, a 2027 guide implying growth under ~15%, or deferred revenue unwinding without converting. It is below the May 2026 post-Q1 lows of $136-142 and roughly one annual sigma below spot, so normal 45-54% volatility alone is unlikely to take the stock there.

reasoning: Round 2, base-rate lane. The supervisor's corrections I accepted: FY27 consensus EPS is $5.20 (29 analysts; FY26 $4.11), replacing my figure backed out of a snippet. Horizon net cash is ~$15/share, not today's $10.5. The Q3 date is unannounced and likely Tue Nov 3. No November analyst day. Microsoft/Meta are 26/16%. Following its feedback, I conditioned my own-history base rate on starting valuation. I rebuilt monthly closes from Dec-2015 to Sep-2026 (Twelve Data) and computed an NTM P/E for each month from split-adjusted annual non-GAAP EPS. The EPS history is approximate, and realized forward EPS carries a hindsight bias. Results: from starting NTM P/E below 30x, the median next-12m return was +66% (n=85, P(<0) 8%). From 30-38x it was +13% (n=31, P(<0) 29%, 10th/90th percentile -24%/+46%). ANET has only ~2 months above 38x, and today it is ~41x. My round-1 unconditioned median of +46% therefore came mostly from cheap starting points, and the supervisor was right that my right tail was too fat. I cut P(>=408) from 7.5% to 5.4% and P(>=510) from 2.5% to 1.6%, and moved the bull price from $310 to $295. Fair value comes out at ~$200. Using consensus EPS and a correct horizon cash figure would raise it. I did not reach the supervisor's $209 because I kept 17% FY28 growth (vs its ~20%), a 35x multiple, and a 38% FCF margin at a 3.25% yield. My FCF margin is lower than the ~40% implied by its ~$7.8B, because H1 OCF excluding the deferred build was only ~22%. The distribution is a 90/10 mixture: a lognormal with median $216 and sigma 0.41, plus a bust component (median $125, sigma 0.35) for a capex-cut or recession outcome. That gives a median of ~$205 (P(>=204) 51%), a mean of ~$220, and a left tail slightly fatter than one lognormal. The analyst mean target of $231-242 is treated as upside-skewed evidence, not the answer. The 1-month sigma is tightened to ~14% on the recent realized vol. Research was limited: Twelve Data's earnings endpoint is paywalled, and historical EPS comes from company annual results, not re-downloaded in this round.
